thread:
lee: FYI hit a confusing failure in local dev while following the Python SDK quickstart. Import fails only when using `poetry install --develop` or `pipx runpip poetry install` but installing the wheel works.

rachel: What does the error look like?

lee: Short repro: after dev install `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient"` -> `ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood'` with unknown location. No problems with `pip install dist/*.whl`.

omar: Sounds like editable metadata vs wheel metadata divergence. What's your pyproject name vs package folder?

lee: pyproject: `name = "redwood-inference"` but source dir is `redwood/`. No explicit `packages` declaration.

rachel: Ah. When PEP 660 editable wheels are not available (old pip/poetry), the editable path relies on setuptools metadata and distribution->package mapping. Wheels bake that mapping so they mask the issue.

ci-bot: CI observed similar failures in job 9012: missing `py.typed` and editable import error. Artifact: https://ci.example/9012/artifacts

sre: Another wrinkle we saw: internal projects sometimes pin `httpx` in their lockfile to an older minor (0.22.x) which causes weird runtime errors in AsyncClient and confuses debugging. Lockfile pinning + editable install bugs = a painful triage loop.

omar: Two fixes: (1) make distribution metadata explicit so editable installs map to `redwood` (e.g., `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` or `packages = ["redwood"]`), (2) include `py.typed` in package_data if we ship typing stubs so `mypy`/editors behave.

rachel: Can we also add a small contributor doc section: "If you use poetry/pipx for dev, ensure pip >= 23 or build a wheel". Save folks from the trap.

lee: Workaround for now: `python -m build && pip install dist/*.whl` or upgrade pip and poetry to support PEP 660. Confirmed that fixed it locally.

ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/1402 76 with repro, CI logs, and suggested pyproject diff.

sre: Suggest adding a CI smoke test that runs `pip install -e .` and `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient"` across mac/linux matrix. Would have caught this pre-merge.

omar: Also proposing we add a short note in the quickstart about recommended local install paths (wheel vs editable) and list minimum pip/poetry versions for PEP 660.

docs: I'll add a Quickstart note and a "Packaging pitfalls" section to the contributor guide.

lee: Thanks. One more gotcha: our backward-compat shim for older httpx used a private attr that changed between 0.22 and 0.23; we should document compatibility and maybe loosen strict pins in our own tests to catch runtime API changes.

rachel: Action items: 1) update pyproject metadata (omar), 2) add py.typed to package_data (omar), 3) add editable-install smoke test to CI (sre), 4) docs quickstart note (docs).

omar: I'll open PR with metadata fix + unit to validate `from redwood import AsyncClient` after editable install.

lee: Cheers, saved me a bunch of time. :thumbsup:
